abstract: This paper investigates how developers conceptualize AI-powered Development Tools and how these role attributions influence technology acceptance. Through qualitative analysis of 38 interviews and a quantitative survey with 102 participants, we identify two primary Mental Models: AI as an inanimate tool and AI as a human-like teammate. Factor analysis further groups AI roles into Support Roles (e.g., assistant, reference guide) and Expert Roles (e.g., advisor, problem solver). We find that assigning multiple roles to AI correlates positively with Perceived Usefulness and Perceived Ease of Use, indicating that diverse conceptualizations enhance AI adoption. These insights suggest that AI4SE tools should accommodate varying user expectations through adaptive design strategies that align with different Mental Models.

ur.tldr: 通过38次访谈与102人问卷，归纳开发者将AI开发工具理解为“工具”或“人类队友”两类心智模型，并细分为支持型与专家型角色。赋予AI多重角色与感知有用性、易用性正相关，建议依据不同心智模型提供自适应设计。

title: AI in Software Engineering: Perceived Roles and Their Impact on Adoption
title_zh: 软件工程中的人工智能：角色认知及其对采纳的影响
